props.title: Build a Ring

B35.capture_spec: C11: Lab square render of lab-shaders/10-disk.gdshader, still. Verified (360x360 Lab): middle 0; d = 0.2 -> 0; d = 0.4 -> 1; corner 1; the disk spans 0.6 of the width (216 of 360 px).
B35.visual_intent: Act title 'Build a Ring' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left (the six-line shader); at right a real Godot window with a square picture: a black disk on white. Read-outs '0' in the disk and '1' outside; a terracotta ring (grey-backed) round the disk's edge at the end.
B35.motion_claim: The distance line, then the step line, are highlighted; the read-outs name the two sides and the ring marks the edge.
B35.why: Predict-then-reveal on the real disk beside two lines of code; the 0 and 1 read-outs name each side.

B36.capture_spec: C12: Lab square render of lab-shaders/11-disk-flip.gdshader, still. Verified (360x360 Lab): middle 1; d = 0.2 -> 1; d = 0.4 -> 0; corner 0. Edge case: step(0.3, 0.3) and step(0.3, 0.3) swapped are both 1 (function-tables: step_args_swapped).
B36.visual_intent: Code card at left (the six-line shader with the arguments swapped); at right a real Godot window with a square picture: a white disk on black. Read-outs '1' inside and '0' outside.
B36.motion_claim: The swapped step line is highlighted; the disk is now white inside; read-outs name the two sides.

show.event: label 'edge first' on the step line

B36.runner_up: manim: the two argument orders side by side
B36.why: The flip is visible in the real render; the code line with the swapped arguments is highlighted.

B37.visual_intent: The standard plot with the input as the distance d from 0 to 0.7 (axis label 'distance'). Curve A: step(0.3, d) in light grey; curve B: step(0.38, d) in mid grey; then the bold curve A − B: a pulse of height 1 between d = 0.3 and 0.38. Mono tag 'ring = step(0.3, d) − step(0.38, d)'. Strip beneath: a bright band in the middle.
B37.motion_claim: Curve A rises at 0.3, curve B rises at 0.38, and their difference is a one-wide pulse that lights a band on the strip.

show.event: midpoint hold: curves A and B settled, the difference not yet drawn
the bold pulse A − B draws; the strip band lit (done by 0.80)

B37.why: A one-dimensional cut through the ring (two steps and their difference) is the cleanest picture of 'cut twice and subtract'.

B38.capture_spec: C13: Lab square render of lab-shaders/12-ring-hard.gdshader, still. Verified (360x360 Lab): d = 0.2 -> 0; 0.34 -> 1; 0.45 -> 0.
B38.visual_intent: Code card at left (the seven-line shader); at right a real Godot window with a square picture: a white ring on black with hard edges. Read-outs '1' on the ring and '0' in the middle; a terracotta ring (grey-backed) round a piece of the hard outer edge at the end.
B38.motion_claim: The ring line is highlighted; read-outs name the mask's one and zero; the ring marks a hard edge.

show.event: ring round a piece of the edge

B38.runner_up: manim: the pulse spun around the middle
B38.why: The real hard ring beside 'step minus step'; the mask is named right where it is visible.

B39.capture_spec: C14: Lab square render of lab-shaders/13-ring-color.gdshader, still. Verified (360x360 Lab): d = 0.2 -> cream (0.9804, 0.9608, 0.9216); 0.34 -> teal (0.3686, 0.6392, 0.5686); 0.45 -> cream.
B39.visual_intent: Code card at left (the nine-line shader); at right a real Godot window with a square picture: a teal ring on a cream background. Labels 'cream' on the background and 'teal' on the ring.
B39.motion_claim: The mix line, then the cream line, then the teal line are highlighted as the voice names them; the two labels land on the picture.

show.event: cream line highlighted; label 'cream' on the background
teal line highlighted; label 'teal' on the ring

B39.why: Real colours at last: the mask decides cream or teal; the picture is the evidence.

B40.capture_spec: C15: Lab square render of lab-shaders/14-ring-soft.gdshader, still. Verified (360x360 Lab): d = 0.2 -> cream; 0.28 -> (0.6941, 0.8118, 0.7569) (half way); 0.34 -> teal; 0.40 -> (0.6431, 0.7843, 0.7255); 0.45 -> cream.
B40.visual_intent: Code card at left (the ten-line shader); at right a real Godot window with a square picture: the same teal ring on cream, now with soft edges. A read-out 'soft' beside the outer edge; a terracotta ring (grey-backed) round the fading inner edge at the end.
B40.motion_claim: The two smoothstep lines are highlighted, then the mix line; the read-out and ring mark the soft edge.

show.event: ring round the fading inner edge

B40.runner_up: ShaderLab hard and soft ring side by side
B40.why: Replacing the two steps by smoothsteps and seeing the soft edge on the real render shows what each function adds.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · radius swept by script

B41.capture_spec: C16: Lab square render of lab-shaders/15-ring-final.gdshader; radius held at 0.30 until 6.0 s, then 0.30 -> 0.12 over 6.0-8.5 s, then 0.12 -> 0.38 over 8.5-11.5 s, held to 12.5 s; 30 fps, Forward+. Verified (360x360 Lab): radius 0.12 -> cream / teal / cream at d = 0.06 / 0.16 / 0.32 ... see lab-summary.txt; radius 0.3 -> teal at d = 0.34; radius 0.38 -> teal at d = 0.42.
B41.visual_intent: Code card at left (the twelve-line finished shader); at right a real Godot window with the soft teal ring from B40 that first holds still, then shrinks and grows as the radius dial is swept. Each highlighted line is named by the voice.
B41.motion_claim: Each function's line lights up as it is named; then the ring grows as the radius is turned.

show.event: full shader visible, ring at rest
the ring grows (the capture holds 0.3 until 6 s)

B41.why: The finished shader, each function highlighted as it is named, beside the ring growing as the radius dial turns, closes the loop with the film's first image.
